name: integration-settings
intro: The settings OpenCTI 7.260811.0-lts.1's integrations read: the 66 every connector shares through pycti, the 22 of the worker, the 1 variables pycti reads for both, and the 100 of XTM Composer. [Run an integration without XTM Composer](/deploy/integrations/manual/) and [Configure XTM Composer](/deploy/integrations/configure-composer/) explain how to set them.

sections.title: Connectors: OpenCTI connection

cells: Extra HTTP headers sent with every API call, as `name:value` pairs separated by `;`, for a reverse proxy or gateway in front of the platform that requires them.
Whether the connector writes its logs as JSON lines (`true`) or as plain text.
Whether the connector checks the platform's TLS certificate; turn it on when the platform URL is HTTPS with a certificate the connector trusts.

API token of the user the connector acts as; with `CONNECTOR_AUTO_CREATE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`, only used to create that account. Give each connector its own user, so that its confidence level and markings apply to what it imports.
URL of the OpenCTI platform the connector registers with and sends its data to, as the connector reaches it (for example `http://opencti:8080` inside a Docker network).

sections.text: Every connector built on pycti reads these settings through its connector helper: the environment variable first, then the key of the connector's `config.yml`, then the default. A connector adds its own settings, listed in its README.

cells: Maximum confidence level (0 to 100) of the service account the connector creates for itself.

Whether the connector creates its own service account at start (`[C] <name>`, in the Connectors group) and uses a fresh token of it; `OPENCTI_TOKEN` must then belong to a user allowed to manage users.
For an enrichment connector, whether the platform also sends it the entities in its scope when they are updated, not only when they are created.
For an enrichment connector, whether the platform sends it every new entity in its scope automatically (`true`) or only when a user asks for an enrichment.
Interval between two runs of a scheduled connector, as an ISO 8601 duration (`PT1H` runs every hour); `0` runs once and stops.
For an enrichment connector, what the platform sends with the entity to enrich: `none` sends the entity alone, `stix_bundle` also sends the bundle of the objects around it.
Whether the connector exposes Prometheus metrics of its activity on `CONNECTOR_METRICS_PORT`.
Unique identifier of the connector (a UUIDv4): the platform keeps the connector's state, works and queue under it. Generate one per connector instance and keep it across restarts.
Path of the HTTP endpoint the connector listens on with the `API` listen protocol.
Port of the HTTP endpoint the connector listens on with the `API` listen protocol.
Certificate (PEM) of the HTTPS endpoint of the `API` listen protocol.
Private key (PEM) of the HTTPS endpoint of the `API` listen protocol.
Passphrase of the private key of the HTTPS endpoint, when the key is encrypted.
Whether the HTTP endpoint of the `API` listen protocol serves HTTPS, with the key and certificate of `LISTEN_PROTOCOL_API_SSL_KEY` and `LISTEN_PROTOCOL_API_SSL_CERT`.
Base URL at which the workers reach the connector's HTTP endpoint with the `API` listen protocol; the connector registers this URL followed by the path. Set it to an address the workers can reach.

How the connector receives the work the platform sends it (enrichments, file imports, exports): `AMQP` from its RabbitMQ queue, or `API` on an HTTP endpoint the worker calls, for a connector that cannot reach RabbitMQ.
For a stream connector, the live stream it reads (its id in the data sharing settings); unset, it reads the raw stream of all events.
For a stream connector, whether it also receives deletion events.
For a stream connector, whether the stream sends the events alone (`true`) or also the objects they depend on.
For a stream connector's first run, the date (ISO 8601) until which the stream replays the existing data before sending live events; unset, the date of the first run.

For a stream connector's first run, the point of the stream to start from, as a stream event timestamp in milliseconds; unset, it starts from the beginning. Ignored once the connector has a saved state.
For a stream connector, whether the stream also sends what the inference rules created.
Level of the connector's logs: `debug`, `info`, `warning` or `error`. Set it to `debug` to investigate a connector, then set it back.
Prefix (Prometheus namespace) of the connector's metric names.
Port of the connector's Prometheus metrics endpoint.
Second prefix (Prometheus subsystem) of the connector's metric names, after the namespace.
Name the platform shows for the connector; also the base of its auto-created service account and of its S3 bundle file names.
For a file import connector, whether it only runs on files attached to an entity (`true`), never on files imported on their own.
How the connector sends its bundles to the platform: `amqp` through the message queue, or `api` through the platform API when the connector cannot reach RabbitMQ.
Former name of `CONNECTOR_QUEUE_PROTOCOL`, read only when that one is not set; the connector logs that it is deprecated.
Size of the connector's queue on the platform, in megabytes, above which a scheduled connector skips its runs until the workers have caught up; raise it for a connector that sends large batches.
Whether the connector runs once and stops, for a connector started by an external scheduler (cron, Kubernetes job) instead of keeping its own schedule.

What the connector handles, comma-separated: entity types for an enrichment connector (`Report,IPv4-Addr`), MIME types for a file import or export connector; the platform offers the connector only for what its scope lists.
Directory the connector writes its bundles to with `CONNECTOR_SEND_TO_DIRECTORY`.
Days the bundle files stay in the directory before the connector deletes them; `0` keeps them.
Whether the connector also writes each bundle as a JSON file to `CONNECTOR_SEND_TO_DIRECTORY_PATH`, to keep the data or move it by other means.
Whether the connector sends its bundles to the platform; turn it off to only write them to a directory or to S3.
Bucket the connector uploads its bundles to; unset, the bucket the platform sends at registration.
Folder (key prefix) of the bucket the connector uploads its bundles to.
Days the connector's bundles stay in the bucket before the connector deletes them.
Whether the connector also uploads each bundle to an S3 bucket, by default the platform's own.

Kind of connector: `EXTERNAL_IMPORT`, `INTERNAL_IMPORT_FILE`, `INTERNAL_ENRICHMENT`, `INTERNAL_ANALYSIS`, `INTERNAL_EXPORT_FILE` or `STREAM`. Set by the connector's own configuration: do not change it.
Whether what the connector sends waits in a workbench or a draft for a user to validate it, instead of being imported directly.
For a file import connector, the XTM One intent it serves: on an automatic import, the platform picks an XTM One agent for this intent when XTM One is configured.
Host of RabbitMQ as the connector reaches it, when it differs from the address the platform sends at registration (a connector outside the platform's network).
RabbitMQ password, to replace the one the platform sends.
Port of RabbitMQ as the connector reaches it, to replace the one the platform sends.
CA certificate (path) that signs RabbitMQ's certificate, for a TLS connection.
Client certificate (path) for a TLS connection to RabbitMQ that requires one.
Private key (path) of the client certificate.
Passphrase of the client certificate's private key.
Whether the TLS connection to RabbitMQ rejects a certificate it cannot verify; turn it on in production.
Whether the connection to RabbitMQ uses TLS, to replace what the platform sends.
RabbitMQ user, to replace the one the platform sends.
RabbitMQ virtual host, to replace the one the platform sends.
Access key for the S3 service, to replace the one the platform sends.
Region of the S3 bucket, to replace the one the platform sends.
Host of the S3 service the connector uploads its bundles to, to replace the one the platform sends.
Port of the S3 service, to replace the one the platform sends.
Secret key for the S3 service, to replace the one the platform sends.
Whether the connector reaches the S3 service over HTTPS, to replace what the platform sends.

sections.title: Worker: OpenCTI connection

cells: Extra HTTP headers sent with every API call, as `name:value` pairs separated by `;`.
Threads that import bundles in parallel in one worker; raise it, or run more workers, when the queues grow and the platform has capacity left.
Whether the worker writes its logs as JSON lines (`true`) or as plain text.
Threads kept for the connectors of the `REALTIME` priority group, so that their work does not wait behind the others.
Seconds the worker waits for an answer of the platform API before it gives up on a call.
Whether the worker checks the platform's TLS certificate.
API token of the user the worker authenticates with.
URL of the OpenCTI platform the worker writes to, as the worker reaches it.

sections.text: The worker reads these settings from its environment first, then from the `config.yml` next to `worker.py`, then the default.

cells: HTTP proxy the worker goes through to call the connectors' HTTP endpoints (`API` listen protocol).
HTTPS proxy the worker goes through to call the connectors' HTTPS endpoints (`API` listen protocol).
Whether the worker checks the TLS certificate of a connector's HTTP endpoint (`API` listen protocol).
Threads that deliver work to the connectors using the `API` listen protocol, by calling their HTTP endpoint.
Level of the worker's logs: `debug`, `info`, `warning` or `error`.

Maximum number of references an object of a bundle may carry; the worker sends an object above it to the dead letter queue instead of importing it. `0` sets no limit; set one to keep huge containers from slowing the import down.
Whether the worker exposes Prometheus metrics (bundles processed, processing time, ingestion units) on `WORKER_PROMETHEUS_TELEMETRY_PORT`.
Address the worker's Prometheus metrics endpoint listens on.
Port of the worker's Prometheus metrics endpoint.
CA certificate (path) that signs RabbitMQ's certificate, for a TLS connection.
Client certificate (path) for a TLS connection to RabbitMQ that requires one.
Private key (path) of the client certificate.
Passphrase of the client certificate's private key.
Whether the TLS connection to RabbitMQ rejects a certificate it cannot verify; turn it on in production.

sections.title: Connectors and worker: pycti environment

cells: CA certificate of an HTTPS proxy that intercepts traffic, as a PEM content or a file path: pycti adds it to the system certificates and trusts the bundle for its calls to the platform.

sections.text: pycti reads these variables from the environment only, in connectors and the worker alike.

sections.title: XTM Composer: manager

cells: Path of the file holding the RSA private key; takes priority over `manager.credentials_key` when both are set.
RSA private key (PEM, 4096 bits) that decrypts the connectors' secret settings the platform sends; set it, or `manager.credentials_key_filepath`, from a secret.
Whether Composer logs the environment variables of each connector it deploys, with the secret values masked, to check what a connector receives.
With `manager.debug.show_env_vars`, whether the logs show the secret values too; only for a short investigation.
Seconds between two passes of Composer over the connectors (deploy, start, stop, update to match the platform); also the wait between two attempts to reach Docker or Podman at start.
Unique identifier of this XTM Composer: the platform lists it under this id and assigns it the connectors it manages. Give each Composer its own id.

Suffix Composer adds to the tag of every connector image it deploys, `-fips` or `-ubi9`, for the FIPS or Red Hat UBI builds of the connectors (`6.9.0` becomes `6.9.0-fips`, an image without a tag `latest-fips`). Any other value stops Composer at start. The FIPS image of Composer sets `-fips`.
In this version, turns on the daily log files of the `logs` folder next to the binary (the code swaps it with `manager.logger.directory`).
In this version, turns on the logs on the standard output (the code swaps it with `manager.logger.console`).
Format of the logs on the standard output: `json` or `pretty`; the log files are always JSON.
Name the platform shows for this XTM Composer.
Seconds between two signals of life Composer sends to the platform.

sections.text: XTM Composer reads `config/default.yaml`, then `config/<COMPOSER_ENV>.yaml` when it exists, then the environment: a variable is the key in upper case with `__` between levels. The `openaev` block takes the same keys as the `opencti` block below (variables `OPENAEV__...`).

cells: Seconds Composer waits to open a connection to the platform.
Whether Composer manages the connectors of an OpenCTI platform.
HTTP proxy URL, with `opencti.with_proxy`; unset, Composer takes `HTTP_PROXY` from its environment.

CA certificates of an intercepting proxy, each a file path or an inline PEM: Composer mounts them in each connector and points `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` and `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` to them.
Whether the connectors reject a proxy certificate they cannot verify; `false` passes `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0` to them.
HTTPS proxy URL, with `opencti.with_proxy`; unset, Composer takes `HTTPS_PROXY` from its environment.
Seconds between two reports of the connectors' logs to the platform, at most.
Hosts reached without the proxy, comma-separated, passed to the connectors; unset, Composer takes `NO_PROXY` from its environment.
Seconds Composer waits for an answer of the platform API.
API token of the user Composer authenticates with on the platform.
Whether Composer accepts a platform TLS certificate it cannot verify; only for a test platform.
URL of the OpenCTI platform, as Composer reaches it.

Whether Composer goes through a proxy to reach the platform and passes the proxy settings (`HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY` and the CA) to the connectors it deploys; off, it ignores every proxy, even the system's.
Orchestrator Composer deploys the connectors on: `kubernetes`, `docker`, `podman`, `swarm` or `portainer`; its block configures it.
Email of the private registry account, when the registry asks for one.
Registry the connector images are pulled from, instead of Docker Hub (a mirror or a private registry).
The same base Deployment as a JSON string, read when `base_deployment` is not set (convenient in an environment variable).
Kubernetes Deployment every connector's deployment starts from (labels, node selectors, security context...), merged under what Composer sets.
When Kubernetes pulls a connector image: `Always`, `IfNotPresent` or `Never`; another value falls back to `IfNotPresent`.
CPU and memory requests and limits of each connector container.
Linux capabilities added to the connector containers.
Linux capabilities removed from the connector containers (`ALL` to harden them).
DNS search domains of the connector containers.
DNS servers of the connector containers.
Extra `host:ip` entries of the connector containers' hosts file.
IPC namespace mode of the connector containers.
Network the connector containers join, usually the network of the OpenCTI stack so that they reach the platform and RabbitMQ.
PID namespace mode of the connector containers.
Whether the connector containers run privileged; leave it off unless a connector needs it.
Container runtime of the connector containers (for example `runsc` for gVisor).
Security options of the connector containers (SELinux labels, seccomp or AppArmor profiles).
Size of the connector containers' `/dev/shm`, in bytes.
Docker API socket (path or `unix://` URL); unset, `/var/run/docker.sock`.
Kernel parameters of the connector containers.
Resource limits of the connector containers, each with a `name`, a `soft` and a `hard` value.
User namespace mode of the connector containers.
UTS namespace mode of the connector containers.
Linux capabilities added to the connector containers.
Linux capabilities removed from the connector containers (`ALL` to harden them).
DNS search domains of the connector containers.
DNS servers of the connector containers.
Extra `host:ip` entries of the connector containers' hosts file.
IPC namespace mode of the connector containers.
Network the connector containers join, usually the network of the OpenCTI stack so that they reach the platform and RabbitMQ.
PID namespace mode of the connector containers.
Whether the connector containers run privileged; leave it off unless a connector needs it.
Container runtime of the connector containers (for example `runsc` for gVisor).
Security options of the connector containers (SELinux labels, seccomp or AppArmor profiles).
Size of the connector containers' `/dev/shm`, in bytes.
Podman API socket (path or `unix://` URL); unset, Composer looks for the rootless socket (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/podman/podman.sock`), then the rootful one.
Kernel parameters of the connector containers.
Resource limits of the connector containers, each with a `name`, a `soft` and a `hard` value.
User namespace mode of the connector containers.
UTS namespace mode of the connector containers.
Linux capabilities added to the connector containers.
Linux capabilities removed from the connector containers.
DNS search domains of the connector containers.
DNS servers of the connector containers.
Extra lines of the connector containers' hosts file, in its own format (`ip host`), unlike the `host:ip` of Docker and Podman.
Whether the connector containers run an init process that reaps child processes.
Overlay network the connector services attach to.
Placement constraints of the connector services (`node.role==worker`).
Spread preferences of the connector services across nodes (`node.labels.zone`).
Whether the connector containers' root filesystem is read-only.
CPU limit of each connector service, in nano CPUs (`1000000000` is one CPU).
CPU reserved for each connector service, in nano CPUs.
Memory limit of each connector service, in bytes.
Memory reserved for each connector service, in bytes.
When Swarm restarts a connector task: `none`, `on-failure` or `any`.
Wait between two restarts of a connector task, in nanoseconds.
Maximum restarts of a connector task; `0` sets no limit.
Time a connector container gets to stop before it is killed, in nanoseconds (`10000000000` is 10 seconds).
Kernel parameters of the connector containers.
Resource limits of the connector containers, each with a `name`, a `soft` and a `hard` value.
User the connector containers run as (`uid:gid`).
Portainer access token Composer authenticates with.
Docker API version Composer calls through Portainer.
Id of the Portainer environment the connectors run in.
Type of the Portainer environment; only `docker` is supported.
Network the connector containers join, usually the network of the OpenCTI stack.
Compose project the connector containers are labelled with, to group them with a stack in Portainer.
Name of a second configuration file Composer reads after `config/default.yaml`: `config/<COMPOSER_ENV>.yaml`, when it exists.
With the `podman` orchestrator and no `socket_path`, where Composer looks for the rootless Podman socket first (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/podman/podman.sock`).
